texts.9252afcb84d7: Objective for processing: The aim of this project is to interrogate the HES APC data and enable benchmarking type comparisons of separate organisations. The raw patient level data will be analysed and aggregated indicators calculated for various key performance indicators e.g. Average Lengh Of Stay (ALOS). The purpose of the request is to enable us and our subscribers to research the relative performance of organisations e.g. ALOS for various specialties, diagnosis and HRG Codes. SSentif Ltd clients are public sector only. They are either NHS and Local Government. Local government organisations are clients as the public health departments require access to NHS data. There is no patient identifiable data available in SSentif, all data is aggregated to a level which is similar to the freely published data available through HSCIC and NHS England. The data will be used to create aggregated indicators to enable comparative benchmarking of organisations. Small number suppression in accordance with the HES analysis guide is applied to all results smaller than 6. Subscribers will not have access to individual record levels. Subscribers only have access to aggregated data levels with small number suppression applied. The output from the data will be aggregated cubed data for all organisations which can then be interrogated/compared. SSentif have been using this restricted HES extract for the last 7 years. Processing activities: The raw individual record data will be held in a secure database which will only be visible to a single person. Software has been developed to interrogate the data and the information derived by the software will be aggregate data only with small numbers suppressed (less than 6). No individual record level data will be visible to anyone except one nominated person and this record level data is pseudonimised. SSentif Ltd have clients across the whole country. SSentif Ltd offer them the ability to create benchmarking groups from anywhere in England so they can compare to organisations with similar department sizes. E.g. a client in the North West can be reviewing data for General Surgery and they can see which hospitals in England have similar numbers of General Surgery patients and then compare ALoS against those hospitals. To do this data is needed for the whole of England. Specific outputs expected, including target date: The outputs will be aggregated indicator values (e.g. ALOS) for all NHS organisations and will be available to be used for benchmarking purposes by subscribers. The outputs are not in record level form. Outputs are ongoing and there is no specific target date. We are constantly requesting and updating the latest information to allow analysis of longitudinal trends. The data is not provided in record level form to any third parties. Expected measurable benefits to health and/or social care including target date: SSentif Ltd subscribers use this data to identify service areas which may need closer attention. For example, they may see the patient numbers for a specific specialty are increasing each quarter/year so they need to plan for more capacity. A Trust may discover that their length of stays are consistently longer than a similar trust and yet the comparable trust has lower readmission rates so they will be keen to learn why there is such a difference. Essentially our subscribers use the aggregated data to identify service areas which may need a closer look and potentially a service redesign. Subscribers also use the data to populate their performance board reports where they require a comparator as well as their own data. These are quotes from clients “We needed a tool which would allow us to look at a range of information, from performance against Government targets, to spending data. We were also particularly interested in looking at spend per head of population as traditionally Lincolnshire has always emerged as a ‘low spender’ and we wanted to look at the expenditure of trusts with similar demographics. “Although that information is already out there, it’s not easy to get to and other systems were only able to offer anonymised data, which was meaningless for our purposes. What SSentif offered was access to everything we needed all in one place.” “The more we use the SSentif system, the more we realise its potential to influence positive change within our organisation.” “The report (using SSentif) was a real eye-opener. It highlighted areas in which – having previously only looked at our own performance – we were both over and under-performing on a national level. When you don’t compare yourself to other organisations, you can become quite inward looking, and there were a number of areas where, although our individual performance may have improved annually, comparatively it became clear there was still some work to be done.” “The SSentif system has allowed us to back up our assertions with facts, to drill down to a greater level of detail that will allow us to make informed decisions in the future and monitor our service to ensure we continue to provide the highest possible level of patient care.” The clients have access to the system on a 12 month rolling contract. Many of Ssentif’s clients have been using the system for a number of years which indicates the benefits the system is giving them. An example of this is Mersey Care who are now in the 5th renewal year. The information in the case studies (available on http://www.ssentif.com/case_studies.shtml from which the quotes were taken) and Ssentif’s client retention shows the benefits to the NHS and local government of our analysis services. YES - the data will be available at non-record level by subscribers via SSentif Ltd software
